subject.summary: A ReVox A77 studio tape recorder with two 10.5-inch reels turning and quarter-inch tape threaded across three heads. Cabinet, reel diameter, tape speed, head count and control layout come from the maker's service manual and a collector's specification; axle spacing, pack radii and the head-cover-off presentation are traced from reference photographs. The tape ribbon is a fixed geometric path while the reels, capstan and pinch roller turn.

identity.feature: two 10.5-inch open reels, wider than the cabinet, almost touching between the spools
stainless name band carrying REVOX / A 77 STEREO TAPERECORDER above the control panel
console under the name band: five lever buttons, four knurled knobs, two VU meters, power switch
quarter-inch tape threaded from the supply pack across three heads past the capstan to the take-up pack

next: Rebuild the three head faces as rectilinear pole pieces with a curved front and a visible gap slit; the cylindrical drums read as rings at close range.
Add the sprung tape-tension arms with rollers that flank the head block on the real deck, and thread the ribbon over them.
Reel windows are wedge gaps between three spokes; the ReVox reel's windows are rounded trapezoids, traceable from the front photograph.
The tape ribbon is a fixed geometric path: the reels, guides and capstan turn but the ribbon itself does not travel. A splice marker would make the transport read as running.
Rear connector panel exists but is simplified; the back view still reads as a plain crate.
